summary: Claus Oetke worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD (~1968–1973) and Habilitation (~1974–1983) at the University of Hamburg, later teaching there, at Kiel, Vienna, and serving as head of Indology at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

An Indologist and Tibetologist, Vogel earned his PhD (~1952–1956) and Habilitation (~1957–1964) at the University of Marburg, also studying at Deccan College. He held professorships at Marburg, Göttingen, and served as Ordinarius at the University of Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She served as Associate Professor in 2007 and held a post from 2020 to 2025 at the University of Canterbury.

Active in Indology and linguistics, Clemens a Jesu studied at the Urban College until 1756. He served in the Archdiocese of Verapoly (~1756–1782) and was appointed General Vicar of the Malabar Mission in 1774.

Markham was active in history, archaeology, and Tibetology after studying at Cheam and Westminster. He served as Assistant Secretary at the India Office (1867–1877), and held secretary and president posts at both the Hakluyt Society and Royal Geographical Society.
Clinton B. Seely was an Indologist who held posts at the University of Chicago, where he is attested in 2007 and attested in 2026 as Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations.
Kluckhohn studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard (~1934–1936). He held academic posts at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Indologist and linguist Colette Caillat studied under Walther Schubring, Louis Renou, and Jules Bloch. She worked at the CNRS, the University of Lyon, and the Sorbonne (1967–1988), and directed the Institut de Civilisation Indienne (~1979–1989).

Colette Sciberras is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her doctorate at Durham University under David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and also studied under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in the fields of philosophy and religious studies who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.

After attending Dollar Academy, Mackenzie worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an engineer in the Madras Engineer Group (1786), Surveyor-General of Madras (1807), and Surveyor General at the Survey of India (1810–1815).
Turnbull was active in Tibetology and other fields. He completed his education at Westminster School (~1938–1942), Magdalen College, Oxford (~1942–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951).

Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, Cox earned her PhD at Columbia under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and studied at Tokyo and Ryukoku universities. She became a professor at the University of Washington in 1985.
Congjun Long works in computational linguistics and Tibetology. Long has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Conor Roddy works in philosophy and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011) under Kathleen Higgins, having also studied under William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.

Bursian worked in history and archaeology after studying at Leipzig and Berlin. He held posts at the universities of Leipzig (~1856–1858), Zurich (~1861–1864), Tübingen (~1864–1869), Jena (~1869–1874), and Munich (~1874–1883).
Conrad M. Arensberg studied at Harvard University (~1927–1934) and served on the faculty at Columbia University from approximately 1946 to 1979.

Kassor studied at Smith College and earned a PhD from Emory (2006–2014) under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock. She held posts at Rangjung Yeshe Institute, Smith College, and Lawrence University (Assistant Professor, 2016).
Constance Powell Chin works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Christian Luczanits and completed a master's degree at San Jose State University, graduating by 2012.

Constant Chounavel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Major Seminary of Saint-Dié. He served in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Jaffna (1852–1883) and was pastor at St. Lucia's Cathedral.
